meta.title: FlatMMO — Practical Skill Guides
meta.sourceBaseline: v2-online 9a9ed99a7e3b35d190c2b2cae47fb05549a1f232; game-data files from this session, not a fresh live-game audit
meta.scope: Guides only; no Companion engine or GitHub changes
meta.policy: Unknown mechanics stay unknown. Source tables are snapshot evidence, not independently refreshed pages. Suggestions are editorial; calculations use explicit recipes/rules.

guides.purpose: Build a working melee setup before chasing a best weapon.

sections.start: Equip a melee-type weapon, then deal melee damage to train. Check the weapon’s Melee requirement separately from the Forging level needed to make it. If you already own a usable weapon, you can begin planning around it without first committing to a production chain.
sections.choose_next: Choose your next target by purpose: a monster drop you need, a quest objective, or a recorded equipment unlock. Check that monster’s listed weakness and physical Defence. A listed weakness improves hit chance and damage, but the available formulas cannot tell us whether the fight is safe or which weapon wins overall.
sections.work_toward: Every ten Melee levels gives a recorded +1 style damage. Treat those as milestones, not a reason to promise a particular kill time. If making Iron Armour is your goal, its full set needs 125 Iron Bars; making and equipping it have different requirements.
sections.if_stuck: If training appears stalled, check Sleep Points. If the fight is going badly, do not interpret “meets the equip requirement” as “ready for this monster”. Exact hit chance, damage rolls, DPS and survival estimates remain unknown.

recordedSkill.name: Melee
recordedSkill.training: Deal melee damage while a melee-type weapon is equipped.
keyRules: 8 XP per point of melee damage dealt
+1 Melee damage per 10 Melee levels
Melee weapon families include swords, scimitars, maces/clubs, knives/spears/tridents.

guides.purpose: Prepare both the weapon and its ammunition.

sections.start: You need a bow and arrows to attack. Arrows are consumed, so check your supply before committing to a training session. Check the equip requirements on both components; owning a bow alone is not a complete setup.
sections.choose_next: Pick a monster for a documented purpose, such as a needed drop, and inspect its weakness and physical Defence. Archery uses that physical Defence field in the current rules. The data does not support assigning a safe enemy or fastest training target from your level alone.
sections.work_toward: Use recorded bow and arrow unlocks as shopping or crafting goals. Crafting can supply Archery equipment, but a Crafting requirement is not an Archery equip requirement. Every ten Archery levels adds +1 style damage.
sections.if_stuck: If you cannot attack, check bow, arrows and equip requirements first. If XP stops, check Sleep Points. We cannot calculate arrows per kill or the ammunition needed for a level target without more combat and XP information.

recordedSkill.training: Attack with a bow and arrows.

guides.purpose: Assemble the complete casting setup before planning training.

sections.start: The recorded setup requires a staff, a Damage Orb and an Element Orb. Check all three before treating a failed attack as a level problem. Staff production and orb production are separate activities: Crafting covers staves, while Enchantment covers orbs.
sections.choose_next: Choose an Element Orb with the intended monster’s documented elemental weakness in mind. Magic attacks use Magic Defence, not the physical Defence field. This gives you a meaningful comparison to inspect, but not a calculated winning setup.
sections.work_toward: If supplying your own orbs, use the Enchantment guide to check base and multiple-output thresholds and shrine access. Keep Magic equip levels separate from Enchantment production levels. Every ten Magic levels adds +1 style damage.
sections.if_stuck: Exact hit chance, damage rolls, DPS and survivability remain unresolved. Do not assume another game’s spellbook, rune costs or recipes. If XP stops while the setup is complete, check Sleep Points.

guides.purpose: Treat Health progression as part of your combat plan.

sections.start: Health XP comes from damage dealt in combat. Choose the combat style you want to develop, assemble its required equipment, and monitor Health alongside that style. The recorded award is 2 Health XP per point of damage dealt.
sections.choose_next: Each Health level increases maximum HP by one. This is a concrete progression benefit, but extra maximum HP alone does not establish which monster you can survive. Enemy accuracy, damage resolution and your complete setup still matter.
sections.work_toward: Use a future Health level as an HP milestone, not as a standalone recommended combat level. The documented normal maximum is 109 HP at Health 100. If your objective is simply to improve a combat style, Health training accompanies damage dealt.
sections.if_stuck: The normal death rule records respawning in Everbrook without item loss. Do not extend that rule to Hardcore or other restricted modes. This snapshot cannot supply a reliable safe-monster list or time-to-level calculation.

recordedSkill.name: Health
recordedSkill.training: Gain Health XP through combat damage dealt.
keyRules: 2 Health XP per point of damage dealt
+1 maximum HP per Health level
documented cap 109 HP

guides.purpose: Plan around an actual task before choosing what to fight.

sections.start: The recorded training activities are hunting tasks and expeditions. Read your available task’s objective and conditions in the game, then make that objective the plan. The current pool does not identify a complete starting NPC, task board or acceptance sequence, so this guide cannot give a verified click-by-click start.
sections.choose_next: For a task involving a named monster, look up its location, weakness and required access, then check your combat setup. That connects Hunting to a concrete objective without assuming every monster or expedition is currently available to you.
sections.work_toward: When considering a task upgrade, inspect what it changes: selection, rewards or behaviour. Those upgrade categories are documented; a complete priced upgrade order is not. Choose based on the obstacle you are actually encountering.
sections.if_stuck: No fastest-task ranking, exact task XP plan, complete upgrade schedule or generic safe combat level is established here. A task name and its in-game description are the most useful missing inputs for a more detailed plan.

recordedSkill.name: Hunting
keyRules: Hunting has unlockable task upgrades
upgrades modify hunt selection/rewards/behaviour

guides.purpose: Separate gaining Worship levels from refilling Worship Points.

sections.start: Bury bones or ashes to train according to the skill record. Cemeteries refill Worship Points. If your immediate problem is an empty point supply, go to a recorded refill location rather than assuming you need another level first.
sections.choose_next: Everbrook Cemetery has a recorded Worship refill service. Omboko Cemetery, Ghost Mansion Cemetery and Frostvale Cemetery also have refill services in the world data. Check area access before choosing a distant refill stop.
sections.work_toward: Choose an ability you want to use—movement, teleporting or another utility action—and check its displayed level and WP cost. Point capacity increases with Worship level, but the pool does not contain a complete normalized ability-cost table or bone-XP table.
sections.if_stuck: Do not import Prayer mechanics or bone values from another game. If you can identify the desired ability and its recorded requirement, that becomes a useful level goal; without it, an exact training quantity would be invented.

recordedSkill.training: Bury bones/ashes and interact with worship mechanics.
keyRules: Worship Points begin at 1 and increase by 1 per Worship level

guides.purpose: Mine toward a material you will actually use.

sections.start: The starting tool is a Bronze Pickaxe. Before travelling, choose a recipe or item goal and identify its ore requirements. Mining consumes Sleep Points, so check that you can restore them before a long gathering session.
sections.choose_next: For a concrete Forging goal, one Bronze Bar requires one Copper Ore and one Coal Ore. One Iron Bar requires one Iron Ore and one Coal Ore. That makes fuel part of your gathering plan, not an optional extra. The item data can identify recorded sources, but missing ore unlock levels must be checked in game.
sections.work_toward: For ordinary ores, every two Mining levels after the ore unlock removes one mining tick; Meteor and Piles use ten-level intervals instead. Better pickaxes also provide speed buffs. Revisit a useful ore as your level improves instead of assuming the newest ore is always the best choice.
sections.if_stuck: The current graph records Graphite at Mining 70 in the Volcano’s Graphite Room, and a Mining-50 access requirement for the Charcoal Wall in Hell. These are later targets, not beginner routes. Exact gathering rates need base ticks and tool details that are not fully normalized.

guides.purpose: Choose the finished item, then work backwards to bars and ore.

sections.start: Smelt bars at a furnace and forge products at an anvil. At Forging 1, Bronze Bars use one Copper Ore plus one Coal Ore each. A Bronze Knife is also recorded at level 1 and uses five Bronze Bars. If you want one knife from raw materials, that is five Copper Ore and five Coal Ore, derived from those recipes.
sections.choose_next: At level 5, Iron Bar smelting becomes a recorded option: one Iron Ore plus one Coal Ore per bar. Smelting a metal does not automatically unlock every item made from that metal. Check the product’s own Forging requirement before gathering a large batch.
sections.work_toward: Full Iron Armour is a concrete project: Forging 25 to make, Melee 10 to equip, and 125 Iron Bars across its five pieces. From ore, that means 125 Iron Ore and 125 Coal Ore. Pick this goal if you want the set; it is not a proven fastest-XP route.
sections.if_stuck: If you already own bars, skip their raw-material gathering. If you cannot make an item, check the station, product requirement, ingredients and Sleep Points. No cheapest or fastest training schedule is established by recipe XP alone.

recordedSkill.name: Forging
keyRules: bars are smelted at a furnace
weapons/armour and other products are forged at anvils
higher-tier metals require increasing fuel/material requirements

guides.purpose: Pick a useful output that matches your available materials.

sections.start: The recorded interface allows left-clicking a log to open recipes. Crafting covers several supply chains, including bows, staves, arrows, armour, vials and gems. Choose the chain that supports your next activity rather than gathering unrelated materials simply because a recipe is unlocked.
sections.choose_next: Arrow Shafts provide a concrete level-1 example: one ordinary Log produces two shafts for 5 recorded XP. Other log recipes produce different quantities. A higher-tier log recipe being craftable at level 1 does not mean you can gather that log at Woodcutting 1.
sections.work_toward: If your goal is Atlas Crown, the recorded quest requirement is Crafting 50 alongside Mining 40. Use your current level and accessible recipes to work toward that gate. The data can give per-recipe inputs; it cannot honestly choose the fastest or cheapest route without complete XP thresholds, timings and prices.
sections.if_stuck: Before making an equipment upgrade, check its equip skill separately from its Crafting level. If materials are missing, identify the exact missing ingredient and its sources. If a recipe offers several input variants, choose one before calculating batch totals.

recordedSkill.name: Crafting
recordedSkill.training: Craft items from logs, hides, bars, gems and other materials.
keyRules: crafting can be started by left-clicking a log to open recipes
products include bows, staves, arrows, armour, vials and gems

guides.purpose: Check the shrine and ingredients before chasing an orb unlock.

sections.start: Damage Orb 1 is recorded at Enchantment 1: one Unpowered Orb produces one Damage Orb 1, with Mystic Vale listed as its location. Confirm shrine access as well as the level. Some shrine access depends on quests or bundles.
sections.choose_next: Grass Orb is recorded at level 5 with Omboko as its location; Water Orb begins at 15 and Fire Orb at 25. These are production milestones. The Magic setup still requires a staff, a Damage Orb and an Element Orb, so plan the complete setup rather than just one orb.
sections.work_toward: Multiple-output thresholds make later levels useful for existing recipes. Damage Orb 1 has base/double/triple thresholds of 1/20/40; Grass Orb has 5/20/35. Use the recorded threshold for the specific orb rather than applying a universal formula.
sections.if_stuck: Mage armour uses Enchantment to make and Magic to equip. Higher recipes can need Stardust and other materials. Do not start a large batch until its full ingredient list and access are confirmed. A missing triple-output value remains unknown.

recordedSkill.name: Enchantment
recordedSkill.training: Enchant unpowered orbs at elemental shrines; enchant/craft mage armour and other enchanted items.
keyRules: Orb recipes have separate base, double-output, and triple-output Enchantment level thresholds.
Stardust is required by higher-tier Damage Orbs and many armour/gem recipes.
Mage-armour crafting uses Enchantment levels that are separate from the Magic level required to equip the armour.
Some shrines require quest/bundle access.

guides.purpose: Choose a fishing spot you can reach and equip for.

sections.start: Fishing requires the spot’s appropriate tool and, where applicable, bait. The current records put an Anchovy spot in Everbrook Town Square, but that source row does not establish its Fishing level or required tool. Check those in game before treating it as an available starter method.
sections.choose_next: For a longer trip, check the destination’s access before buying supplies. The graph records Anglerfish in Omboko’s Dungeon Anglerfish room with a Fishing Rod requirement, and Eels in the Sewer and Thieves Hideout. Those locations are options to investigate, not an ordered levelling route.
sections.work_toward: Link your fishing goal to what you intend to do with the catch. If you want cooked food, check the corresponding Cooking requirement and preparation method rather than assuming catching it means you can cook it.
sections.if_stuck: Fishing consumes Sleep Points. If XP stops, check that resource before replacing equipment. Missing fish levels, catch rates and complete tool/bait requirements prevent a supported fastest-XP or fish-per-hour guide.

recordedSkill.name: Fishing
recordedSkill.training: Use fishing spots with the required fishing tool/bait.
keyRules: fishing consumes Sleep Points
different fish require different tools/locations/levels

guides.purpose: Choose a crop for both its use and when you can return.

sections.start: At Farming 1, the recorded crop options include Wheat and Barley with 7m 30s growth timers, and Blue, Green and Red Mushrooms with 30-minute timers. Obtain the correct seeds and check access to a plot before planning repeated harvests.
sections.choose_next: If your next goal is Brewing, choose ingredients for a specific potion. A level-1 Melee Potion needs Dotted Green Leaf and Red Mushroom, so growing mushrooms supplies only part of that recipe. Check the remaining ingredient’s acquisition route too.
sections.work_toward: Tree growing is a separate longer-term option: Normal Tree is recorded at Farming 5, requiring 10 bonemeal and five hours of growth. Oak Tree is level 10, 50 bonemeal and ten hours. These are recorded timers, not a proven ranking of XP efficiency.
sections.if_stuck: The skill record lists eight plots including four Greenhouse plots; Greenhouse progression depends on Farmer Bundle and contract points. Straw Hat’s +10 effective levels apply when harvesting—do not treat them as permission to plant ten levels above your actual level.

recordedSkill.training: Plant and harvest crops, trees and fruit at farming plots, and complete Farming contracts.
keyRules: There are 8 documented plots: Everbrook, Mystic Vale, Omboko, Ghost Mansion cemetery, and 4 Greenhouse plots.
Crops have real-time growth timers.

guides.purpose: Decide whether your logs are for Crafting, Firemaking or another recorded use.

sections.start: You need an axe to chop trees. Choose a tree whose requirement you meet, then keep its logs for your planned output. For example, ordinary Logs can become Arrow Shafts through a level-1 Crafting recipe; Firemaking uses logs and matches.
sections.choose_next: Tree tiers include normal, oak, willow and maple before later types, but the current pool does not provide a complete numeric unlock and tool table. Check the tree’s displayed requirement before treating a named world location as a training option.
sections.work_toward: Higher Woodcutting levels and better axes improve chopping speed. That supports checking tool upgrades when gathering becomes a bottleneck, but it does not establish that every higher-tier tree is faster XP. Mining’s tick formula must not be reused for Woodcutting.
sections.if_stuck: If you want access through Omboko’s Cemetery Wall, the recorded gate is a Machete and Woodcutting 80. That is a specific later access goal. Tree locations in the reference section are recorded locations only, with access and unlock gaps left visible.

recordedSkill.name: Woodcutting
keyRules: tree tiers progress from normal/oak/willow/maple and beyond
higher levels/tools improve access and speed

guides.purpose: Build a fire for an intended use, then choose the logs.

sections.start: The recorded training action is lighting logs with matches. Gather both supplies before selecting a place to light the fire. Fires can be made on many world tiles, but not teleport tiles.
sections.choose_next: If you are preparing ordinary food, Cooking records fires as the cooking method. If you are making pies, plan an oven instead. This distinction prevents spending supplies on a fire that does not serve the recipe you intended.
sections.work_toward: Log types have different burn times and XP. Choose a log whose displayed requirements you meet and whose burn time suits the task. The current pool lacks the complete numeric table needed to recommend a levelling order or calculate logs needed for a target level.
sections.if_stuck: If fire creation fails, check your logs, matches and tile first, then inspect the in-game requirement and Sleep Points. Do not assume Woodcutting unlock levels are also Firemaking unlock levels.

recordedSkill.training: Light fires using logs and matches.
keyRules: fires can be made in many world tiles but not teleport tiles

guides.purpose: Choose the dish before choosing the cooking station.

sections.start: Ordinary raw food is cooked on fires; pies use ovens. Start with a food recipe whose requirement and ingredients you can verify. The current pool has explicit pie recipes, but not a complete starter fish-cooking progression.
sections.choose_next: Apple Pie is recorded at Cooking 5 and produces one pie from 20 Apples, 10 Wheat, 10 Sugarcane and five Chicken Eggs. Before gathering, subtract ingredients you already own. For two pies, double those quantities; that is a material calculation, not an XP or profit recommendation.
sections.work_toward: Banana Pie is a recorded level-10 option, Avocado Pie level 15 and Pineapple Pie level 20. Choose a next recipe because its ingredients are accessible and its output is useful. A higher requirement does not prove better training efficiency.
sections.if_stuck: Special potion-created fires or ovens can improve speed, but this pool does not establish a complete timing or burn-chance model. If cooking is blocked, check station type, recipe level, ingredients and Sleep Points.

recordedSkill.training: Cook raw food on fires and use ovens for recipes such as pies.
keyRules: fires cook ordinary food
ovens support pie cooking

guides.purpose: Choose a potion that supports the activity you are about to do.

sections.start: Melee Potion is a fully recorded level-1 example: one Vial, three Dotted Green Leaf and ten Red Mushrooms produce one potion for 75 XP. Its recorded effect is +5 Melee Damage. Make it for that purpose rather than assuming it is the best training recipe.
sections.choose_next: At Brewing 3, Archery Potion uses one Vial, four Dotted Green Leaf and ten Green Mushrooms. Magic Potion is recorded at level 5. Check the full recipe row before collecting supplies; the item graph contains more complete rows than some older skill summaries.
sections.work_toward: Potion duration is recorded as five minutes plus 30 seconds per Brewing level. At level 10, that gives ten minutes, derived from the rule. The duration rule does not apply to beverages. Fermenting unlocks at Brewing 10 and is a distinct process to inspect.
sections.if_stuck: Mining and Woodcutting Potions are recorded later options, but a vague “gathering boost” label is not enough to calculate an exact time saving. Choose effects with documented relevance to your goal; profit and fastest-XP rankings remain unestablished.

recordedSkill.name: Brewing
recordedSkill.training: Brew potions from vials, crops/leaves/mushrooms and use the fermenting system for beverages.
keyRules: Each potion begins with 5 minutes duration and gains 30 seconds per Brewing level.
Potion-duration scaling does not apply to beverages.
Fermenting unlocks at Brewing 10.
Brewing recipes can improve combat, gathering, production and utility activities.

guides.purpose: Choose the kind of source first: pickpocket, stall or chest.

sections.start: Citizen is a recorded level-1 pickpocket target in Everbrook at the Mayor’s house. The source has item-specific drops, including food, logs and seeds. This is a concrete starting target to investigate, not a claim of guaranteed success or optimal XP.
sections.choose_next: Farmer pickpocketing is recorded at Stealing 10 in Everbrook’s Farm. If you need Green Leaf Seeds, that target is one recorded non-combat acquisition route. Farmer also exists as a monster; make sure you are choosing the pickpocket interaction.
sections.work_toward: Choose later targets by the item you want and the access you have. Some stalls have guards; Silent Gloves bypass some guard requirements, not every possible guard or access condition. Chests can have separate access gates.
sections.if_stuck: The unlock level is not a no-failure threshold. Recorded loot odds are not automatically the chance your stealing attempt succeeds, and they do not establish items per hour. The pool does not support a complete success-rate or fastest-training route.

recordedSkill.name: Stealing
recordedSkill.training: Pickpocket NPCs, steal from stalls and open stealable chests.
keyRules: some stalls are guarded
Silent Gloves can bypass some guard requirements

guides.purpose: Choose a movement or Dodge milestone that solves a problem for you.

sections.start: The skill records agility tracks and dodging as training activities. Dodge is available at level 1 and avoids the next attack, with a recorded base cooldown of 60 seconds. The pool does not supply a complete starting-track location and XP schedule.
sections.choose_next: If travel is your main frustration, Agility 20 is a clear target: unlimited running outside combat. Run is measured in steps and is separate from Sleep Points. More Run capacity is not a substitute for restoring Sleep Points when XP stops.
sections.work_toward: For combat utility, level 30 adds a second Dodge slot; level 40 allows Run during combat; level 50 adds another Dodge slot. At 60, a successful Dodge allows an attack on the next possible tick. At 70, the recorded Dodge cooldown is 40 seconds.
sections.if_stuck: Pick the milestone that matters to you, then use an accessible training activity whose requirements you can verify. Exact level-1–19 Run-step scaling, fastest-track progression and a numerical survival benefit from Dodge are not established here.

recordedSkill.name: Agility
keyRules: Agility grants movement/dodge progression
documented passive unlocks include permanent running outside combat at level 20 and running during combat at level 40
